section_summary: This section covers the recovery of Japan’s cotton, knitted-goods, and silk industries, including production figures, fuel and raw-material shortages, and plans for textile exports. It also records negotiations over textile exports to Siam and a dispute over how Japanese silk should be tested, marketed, and sold. A long submission by silk adviser Peter F. Magagna argues for a planned raw-silk export program and changes to the role of the United States Commercial Company.

subfiles.title: Further Press Comment on Japanese Textile Production
subfiles.about: Reports low Japanese textile output and projected rayon growth.
subfiles.summary: Concludes a despatch on cotton supplies, fuel priorities, labor, and textile production forecasts.

subfiles.title: Textile Industry in Japan: Shortage of Fuel Supply
subfiles.about: Describes coal and transport shortages threatening Japanese textile production.
subfiles.summary: Reports output plans and the coal shortage facing textile mills.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for Bombay despatch 2966
subfiles.about: Routes a Bombay consular despatch within the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Lists offices and copy distribution.

subfiles.title: Production of Textiles by Former Japanese-owned Mills in China
subfiles.about: Transmits a report on former Japanese cotton mills operating in China.
subfiles.summary: The mills reportedly run at 10–20 percent capacity because of raw-material shortages; transfer to private industry is planned after two years.

subfiles.title: Clipping on former Japanese-owned textile mills in China
subfiles.about: Provides the press item enclosed with despatch 2966.
subfiles.summary: Only fragments of the clipping are legible.

subfiles.title: Japanese Textile Exports to Siam
subfiles.to: U.S. Legation, Bangkok; Department of State
subfiles.about: Sets out proposed negotiations and shipping terms for Japanese textile exports to Siam.
subfiles.summary: SCAP requests the textile mission’s authority, explains allocation of cotton fabrics, and proposes interim title, receipt, and shipping arrangements.

subfiles.title: Reply to William N. Chase
subfiles.about: Replies to Chase’s July 23 request; the substantive reply is illegible.
subfiles.summary: A short State Department reply with little legible body text.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for Bombay despatch 3000
subfiles.about: Routes Bombay despatch 3000.
subfiles.summary: Lists action office and copy distribution.

subfiles.title: Japanese Export of Knitted Goods
subfiles.about: Encloses a press article on wartime decline in Japanese knitted-goods production.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes restrictions, machinery losses, labor mobilization, and the difficulty of rebuilding an export-oriented industry.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Exports of Knitted Goods
subfiles.about: Presents production and export figures for Japanese knit goods.
subfiles.summary: Describes wartime restrictions and machinery losses, with comparative production tables.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for Bombay despatch 3006
subfiles.about: Routes Bombay despatch 3006.
subfiles.summary: Lists action office and copy distribution.

subfiles.title: Japanese Silk Production
subfiles.about: Encloses figures on Japanese raw-silk and cocoon production.
subfiles.summary: Reports rising May silk output, increased operable reeling basins, a smaller spring cocoon crop, and a projected shortfall against annual requirements.

subfiles.title: Silk Production in Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese silk-industry statistics and the cocoon forecast.
subfiles.summary: Gives April–May production figures and forecasts a cocoon shortfall.

subfiles.title: Authority of Siamese Textile Mission
subfiles.about: Requests confirmation that Siam’s mission can finalize negotiations with SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Seeks clarification of the mission’s negotiating authority.

subfiles.title: Siamese Response on Japanese Textile Exports
subfiles.about: Conveys Siam’s response to SCAP’s proposed textile-export arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Siam accepts two terms, asks SCAP for shipping assistance, and proposes exchanging Siamese goods for textiles.

subfiles.title: Distribution of Textile Mission Report
subfiles.about: Asks when the Textile Mission to Japan report will be published.
subfiles.summary: Rose cites demand from industry and government and renews an offer to distribute the report through the Textile Research Institute.

subfiles.title: Reply on Textile Mission Report
subfiles.about: Explains the delay in printing the Textile Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Whitman expects completion within three weeks and promises to notify Rose.

subfiles.title: British Parliamentary Question on Japanese Textile Export Prices
subfiles.about: Transmits a British parliamentary exchange on control of Japanese textile-export prices.
subfiles.summary: The reply says price controls are handled through occupation and Far Eastern Commission arrangements.

subfiles.title: Article on Japanese Cotton Yarn Production
subfiles.about: Encloses an article on Japanese cotton-yarn and cloth output.
subfiles.summary: Reports lower May yarn production from cotton shortages, higher cloth output, and expected improvement following American cotton arrivals.

subfiles.title: Cotton Yarn in Japan
subfiles.about: Gives Japanese cotton-industry production figures and export prospects.
subfiles.summary: Tabulates April–May yarn and cloth output and anticipates exports after cotton imports arrive.

subfiles.title: Letter on Japanese Silk Policy and Peter Magagna
subfiles.about: Urges review of Japanese silk marketing and the United States Commercial Company’s role.
subfiles.summary: Flood forwards Magagna’s correspondence and program, describes concerns about silk testing and sales, and proposes a conference among government agencies and U.S. silk-industry representatives.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Declining Silk Prices
subfiles.about: Warns that falling silk prices and limited throwing capacity threaten market recovery.
subfiles.summary: Advocates orderly silk sales and direct contact with Japanese reelers under SCAP control.

subfiles.title: Letter on the Occupation Economy and Silk Trade
subfiles.about: Criticizes occupation economic administration and proposes changes to Japanese textile exports.
subfiles.summary: Magagna argues that food shortages, weak coordination, unrealistic exchange rates, and United States Commercial Company procedures impede recovery. He disputes reported export-account figures and silk testing practices, proposes civilian trading organizations and barter, and urges stronger civilian direction of SCAP’s economic work.

subfiles.title: Undated Letter on the United States Commercial Company
subfiles.about: Calls for replacement or reform of the United States Commercial Company’s export role.
subfiles.summary: Magagna alleges that its procedures immobilize silk stocks and distort SCAP accounts. He proposes direct, supervised marketing and a larger civilian role in managing Japan’s economy.

subfiles.title: Report and Recommendations on Rehabilitation of Japanese Raw Silk Industry
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Proposes a coordinated production and export program for Japanese raw silk.
subfiles.summary: Magagna presents raw silk as a major source of foreign exchange and warns against concentrating production on a shrinking hosiery market. He recommends stable prices, regular shipments in marketable grades, wider export eligibility, and consolidated testing at Yokohama. He also calls for production targets, consultations with Allied buyers, fair payment to growers, and coordinated Japanese and SCAP silk administration.

subfiles.title: Policy Telegram on Japanese Silk Production
subfiles.about: Sets policy balancing food production against silk’s foreign-exchange value.
subfiles.summary: Leaves mulberry acreage to SCAP pending firmer import and export targets.

subfiles.title: SCAP Request for Silk Advisers
subfiles.about: Requests Paolino Gerli and Mr. Douty as temporary advisers on Japanese silk.
subfiles.summary: Seeks advice on technical standards, production, prices, and stabilization.

subfiles.title: Raw-Silk Price Decontrol
subfiles.about: Notifies Flood that an order decontrolling raw silk has been signed.
subfiles.summary: Bowles says the order has been sent for official publication.

subfiles.title: Reply on Silk Price Exemption
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the action on silk-price exemption.
subfiles.summary: Flood thanks Bowles and supports the exemption.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Magagna on Silk Sales
subfiles.about: Reports agreement that the United States Commercial Company will not auction silk.
subfiles.summary: Flood reaffirms support for Magagna’s proposals.

subfiles.title: Press Clipping on Silk Demand and Prices
subfiles.about: Discusses expected demand and price behavior after silk controls are lifted.
subfiles.summary: Forecasts strong demand and possible sharp price increases for silk goods.

subfiles.title: Sources for Silk Statistics
subfiles.about: Lists statistical sources used for the silk report.
subfiles.summary: Names U.S., Japanese, exchange, industry, and published sources.

subfiles.title: Advantages of a Single Raw Silk Testing House at Yokohama
subfiles.about: Recommends centralizing official Japanese raw-silk testing at Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Argues that one facility would produce consistent tests, simplify supervision, reduce costs, and use Yokohama’s existing capacity and port access.

subfiles.title: Export Program for Silk Fabrics and Rayon Fabrics
subfiles.to: Chief, Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ, SCAP
subfiles.about: Questions the feasibility of exporting large quantities of Japanese silk fabrics under foreign tariffs.
subfiles.summary: Urges curtailing silk-fabric production and exporting raw silk to earn dollars.
